_comment: Named shopping regions, mapped to the store locations that sit in them. Data rather than code, like feasibility.json and freshness.json: which suburb belongs to which part of Auckland is local knowledge, not a fact derivable from the catalogue, and someone who knows the city should be able to correct it without reading Python.
_why_locations_and_not_coordinates: A region resolves to a SET OF STORE LOCATIONS, not to a centre and a radius. Two reasons, and the second is the binding one. First, a shopper saying 'North Shore' means the shops on the Shore, not everything within N kilometres of an arbitrary midpoint — a radius drawn around Takapuna reaches across the harbour bridge. Second, the 3,000-record dataset in datasets/ carries no lat or lon at all, only store_name, so a coordinate filter cannot run against it however well specified. Radius scope still exists for clients that DO send coordinates; the two intersect when both are given.
_source: datasets/DATA_SCHEMA.md section 1 pairs ten Auckland stores 1:1 across five regions. The fixture catalogue uses six different suburbs, so both sets are mapped here — a region must resolve against whichever catalogue is loaded, or it works in the demo and fails in production.
_matching: Aliases are matched against the user's message case-insensitively on word boundaries. A suburb name is an alias for its own region, so 'near Albany' and 'North Shore' both resolve, which is what the demo scenarios actually ask.
_on_unknown_regions: A region we cannot map is NOT silently ignored. Ignoring it would answer a request about Whangarei with prices from Auckland and give no sign that the location was dropped — the same failure shape as widening a radius back to national. An unrecognised region is reported to the user.
_review: Not reviewed by anyone with local knowledge of Auckland retail geography. The pairings come from DATA_SCHEMA.md and the suburb-to-region assignments from general knowledge; Mt Wellington and Remuera in particular sit near boundaries people argue about. Correcting an entry here needs no code change, which is the point.
